title: Navvi input
description: Describe what to extract and where. A plain-English prompt is enough; the structured fields below pin the details when a program is calling. The second run of the same prompt on the same site replays the compiled scraper with no model call.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: What to extract, in plain words, for example: 'every job on the listing: title, company, location, date posted, link'. Optional when mode and fields are given. Never put credentials in the prompt.
prompt.sectionDescription: Say what you want. Navvi turns the prompt into mode, fields and description through one chooser question; the structured fields below override it.

startUrls.title: Start URLs
startUrls.description: Pages to scrape (http or https, public hosts only). A 'Text file' or 'requestsFromUrl' entry is a URL that answers the page list itself, as newline-delimited text or JSON (an array of URLs or of { url } objects, or an object whose urls, data or items is one), so a backend endpoint can feed the daily target list. A URL whose path ends in .txt, .json or .csv is fetched as a list too.
startUrls.sectionDescription: Where the records are. One template (a listing, or many pages of the same shape) compiles once.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: list: many rows per page (a listing, search results). record: the values of each start URL (a product page, a profile). Derived from the prompt when omitted.

description.title: What the records are
description.description: One phrase naming the records, for example 'python job listing' or 'pharmacy product'. Used in the compile questions; derived from the prompt when omitted.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: The fields to extract. Each needs a name (an identifier); an optional description helps the chooser; an optional type coerces the value after extraction: money and number read '$ 6.990' as 6990 and '12.990,50' as 12990.5, integer takes a whole number, boolean maps stock phrases in Spanish and English (En stock, Agotado, Out of stock), url resolves to an absolute http(s) URL. A value that does not coerce is null. The type is recorded in the compiled scraper so replays coerce the same way.

name.title: Name
name.description: Identifier: letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the value is, when the name alone is ambiguous.

type.title: Type
type.description: Output type the run coerces to; text (the default) keeps the extracted string.

fields.sectionDescription: Named fields with optional output types. Omit them to let the prompt decide.

goal.title: Navigation goal
goal.description: Steps before extracting, in plain words: 'search for python jobs', 'open the Remote category'. The navigator drives the page with the chooser and records the trace; a replay repeats it with no model call. Leave empty when the start URLs are the target pages. The published actor runs the read-only 'store' profile: no logins, no secrets.
goal.sectionDescription: Optional navigation before extraction, and detail pages after it.

followDetailPages.title: Follow detail pages
followDetailPages.description: In list mode, also open each row's detail page and read the detail fields there. Every detail page counts as a scraped page.

detailFields.title: Detail fields
detailFields.description: Fields read on each detail page, same shape as Fields.

maxPages.title: Max pages
maxPages.description: Pages to scrape per template, pagination and detail pages included.
maxPages.sectionDescription: Caps on pages and items. Every run also has a fixed chooser budget: 1.5M chooser input tokens, 40 text-helper calls, 5 healing events, 30 navigation steps.

maxItems.title: Max items
maxItems.description: Dataset items to produce, over every template.

browser.title: Browser
browser.description: Leave empty to use the build's browser (Chromium on the default image, Camoufox on the Camoufox image). Camoufox passes more bot checks on a residential proxy; Chromium is faster.
browser.sectionDescription: The browser and the proxy the pages are opened with.

proxy.title: Proxy
proxy.description: Apify Proxy or your own proxy URLs. A residential proxy is the answer to blocked_bot_detection.

allowedDomains.title: Allowed domains
allowedDomains.description: Domains the crawl may follow beyond the start URLs' registrable domains (next-page and detail links).

chooser.title: Chooser
chooser.description: Both roles at once, the older single field: it sets the Decider and leaves the Writer derived. jev: TypeSafe's System One model through Vercel AI Gateway or a TypeSafe key, the measured default. model: a text model (Claude Haiku) answering a JSON schema of indices. Leave empty to follow the key: jev with a TypeSafe or Gateway key, model with an Anthropic key. Decider and Writer win over it.
chooser.sectionDescription: Two sources, chosen independently: a decider for the structured questions and a writer for the free text. Bring your own key and the operator pays no model cost on your run; without one the actor uses the operator key and the actor-start price covers it. Keys are used for this run only, never stored.

decider.title: Decider
decider.description: Which source answers the structured questions: pick one of the candidates Navvi enumerated, yes/no, or a score. jev: TypeSafe's System One model, the measured default. model: a text model (Claude Haiku) answering a JSON schema of indices. Wins over Chooser when both are set; leave empty to follow Chooser, then the key.

writer.title: Writer
writer.description: Which source answers the free-text questions, such as the search query to type into a box. Jev judges but cannot write. On the platform only the metered API model can write: the Claude Code and Codex CLIs are a local-only feature and no CLI is installed in the actor image. Leave empty to let the decider write, or, under jev, the API model.

deciderTransport.title: Decider transport
deciderTransport.description: Which API the jev decider is reached over: typesafe is the official TypeSafe API (api.typesafe.ai), gateway is the Vercel AI Gateway route. Leave empty to follow the key, gateway first when both are given; set typesafe to force the TypeSafe API even with a Gateway key.

typesafeApiKey.title: TypeSafe API key
typesafeApiKey.description: Your TypeSafe key for the jev chooser (direct provider).

gatewayApiKey.title: Vercel AI Gateway key
gatewayApiKey.description: Your AI Gateway key; jev runs through the gateway's typesafe-ai/jev route, model through its Anthropic route.

anthropicApiKey.title: Anthropic API key
anthropicApiKey.description: Your Anthropic key for the model chooser.

scriptId.title: Pinned scraper (scriptId)
scriptId.description: Replay exactly this compiled scraper instead of looking the cache up: the key in the scraper store (the SUMMARY of a run names it), or 'storeIdOrName/key'. The run then makes no chooser call unless the page drifted and healing is needed.

scraperStore.title: Scraper store
scraperStore.description: The key-value store holding the pinned scraper; defaults to the named store scraper-cache in your account. Used when scriptId is a bare key.

forceRecompile.title: Force recompile
forceRecompile.description: Ignore the cached scraper and compile again (one chooser round). Off for scheduled runs.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: The published actor runs the read-only store profile only: no form submits, no logins, no secrets, no destructive-looking controls. Logins are a local CLI feature.

freshProfile.title: Fresh browser profile
freshProfile.description: Discard the persisted browser profile for the start URLs' domain before the run.
